availableCommands.name: create-release-branch
availableCommands.description: Create a shared Junie CLI and ACP release branch through TeamCity and create its YouTrack Release issue.

availableCommands.name: spec-take-next
availableCommands.description: Pick the first feature with no spec from INDEX.md and autonomously draft it.

availableCommands.name: spec-list
availableCommands.description: List all feature specs and surface drift between docs/specs/ and docs/specs/INDEX.md.

availableCommands.name: spec-loop
availableCommands.description: Run /spec:take-next in a cycle until every feature in INDEX.md has a spec.

availableCommands.name: get-next-release
availableCommands.description: Find the next planned Junie Release issue in YouTrack and report its synchronization state and readiness.

availableCommands.name: release-cli-tickets
availableCommands.description: Prepare tickets for new Junie CLI changes in an existing release branch regardless of their state and synchronize them with its existing YouTrack Release issue.

availableCommands.name: spec-update
availableCommands.description: Update an existing feature spec to reflect a behavior change and refresh INDEX.md.

availableCommands.name: spec-deprecate
availableCommands.description: Deprecate a feature spec, move it to docs/specs/deprecated/, and update INDEX.md.

availableCommands.name: spec-inter
availableCommands.description: Interactively author a new feature spec under docs/specs/ and update INDEX.md.

availableCommands.name: spec-auto
availableCommands.description: Autonomously draft a new feature spec from real artifacts and update INDEX.md.

availableCommands.name: recap
availableCommands.description: Generate a personal GitHub activity summary for you.

availableCommands.name: $a2ux-events
availableCommands.description: Use when need to add or change a2ux events — the typed messages exchanged between the agent and the UI (agent→UI events and UI→agent requests/responses). Apply whenever the Agent ↔ UI interaction contract changes. The contract is declared in a Kotlin DSL schema and the typed SDK is code-generated, so edit the schema and regenerate — never hand-edit the generated files.

availableCommands.name: $acp-custom-llm-endpoints
availableCommands.description: Architecture and invariants for ACP custom LLM provider endpoints in Junie CLI. Use when changing providers/list, providers/set, providers/disable, AcpProxySource, or ACP proxy routing and model visibility.

availableCommands.name: $acp-extensions
availableCommands.description: Use when turning an IJAI ACP requirement into a JUNIE ticket, adding, changing or reviewing an ACP extension method or `_meta` key, re-checking Junie's ACP coverage gaps, or reconciling docs/acp-extensions.md with AIR; not for writing ACP tests or the providers/* contract.

availableCommands.name: $add-new-skill
availableCommands.description: Create or substantially revise a project skill under .agents/skills with portable frontmatter, a precise discovery description, focused instructions, and only the supporting resources the workflow needs.

availableCommands.name: $agent-notes
availableCommands.description: Use when you want to show something to the user in their JetBrains IDE with the AgentNotes plugin — notes on exact lines of code, markdown documents whose links open the code, or reviews and overviews stored in gg — and when the user pastes a link copied from the Agent Notes tool window. Describes what the plugin shows and the exact formats; not what to write.

availableCommands.name: $air-agentic-tests
availableCommands.description: Launch TeamCity Air Plugin + IDE Agentic Testing for Air regression testing, exploratory UI tests, or new LLM model release verification. After every successful queue, immediately post build id + webUrl to the user before any poll. Not for in-process ACP integration tests.

availableCommands.name: $air-plugin-specs
availableCommands.description: Locate, read, and apply AIR Plugin behavior specs under ultimate/plugins/air/spec. Use when Junie work must align with AIR (Agent Threads), ACP live mapping, sessions tree, subagents, launch, frame, or any AIR UX/contract — especially when AIR is the priority surface over AI Chat.

availableCommands.name: $backend-architecture
availableCommands.description: Clean Architecture and Dependency Inversion rules for Kotlin Spring Boot backends. Apply when adding or changing controllers, service contracts, outbound integrations, transparent relays, expected-error handling, application YAML configuration, or boundary tests.

availableCommands.name: $chat-orchestrator-architecture
availableCommands.description: Use when changing the long-lived chat agent session in ej-core `agent/agents/chatMainAgent` — the inbox and its partitions, message kinds, intake of host facts and user input, the runner and its executors, step results and how they become state changes, the state store and its views, history preparation or compression, or restore of a `ChatMainAgentState` snapshot. Not for the classic single-task main agent loop or CLI session events.

availableCommands.name: $cherry-pick-to-release
availableCommands.description: Use when cherry-picking commits into a Junie release branch through a pull request without modifying or stashing the user's current worktree.

availableCommands.name: $claude-api
availableCommands.description: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. TRIGGER when: code imports anthropic/@anthropic-ai/sdk; user asks to use the Claude API, Anthropic SDKs, or Managed Agents (/v1/agents, /v1/sessions, /v1/environments). DO NOT TRIGGER when: code imports `openai`/other AI SDK, general programming, or ML/data-science tasks.

availableCommands.name: $coroutines-and-dispatchers
availableCommands.description: Use when changing Kotlin coroutine scopes, dispatchers, blocking I/O, long-lived network streams or filesystem watchers, coroutine-backed state, or coroutine tests.

availableCommands.name: $create-release-epic
availableCommands.description: Create a Junie YouTrack Release issue for a verified Junie release branch, then synchronize its links and generated body. Use after create-release-branch or when equivalent branch metadata is supplied.

availableCommands.name: $database-connection-management
availableCommands.description: Managing datasources/database connections for DataGrip and other JetBrains IDEs. Use when you need to create, edit, or test datasources/database connections, listing configured data sources, and verifying connectivity.

availableCommands.name: $demo-setup
availableCommands.description: Fill in a project's `/demo` configuration by inspecting the project: complete the `.junie/vms/<vm>/Dockerfile` and the launch command in `.junie/demo.md`. TRIGGER when: the user asks to set up, configure, or finish `/demo`; the user asks you to fill in `.junie/demo.md` or a `.junie/vms/*/Dockerfile`; a first `/demo` run just seeded starter files and aborted. DO NOT TRIGGER when: `/demo` is already configured and the user only wants to run it, or when editing application code unrelated to demo setup.

availableCommands.name: $dispatching-ticket-worker
availableCommands.description: Use when the user gives a ticket or issue URL and asks to start, spawn or dispatch a worker agent for it — to investigate the ticket (mode investigate) or to fix it (mode fix) in a recycled gg worktree on a branch named by the user's prefix scheme. Requires running inside a gg console (gg agent works only there).

availableCommands.name: $docs-review
availableCommands.description: Review Junie documentation/topics pages (typically AI-generated) for tone/terminology, common issues, inconsistencies, and mistakes, premature exposure of non-GA features, and formatting. Use after creating or editing a doc page.

availableCommands.name: $ej-integration-tests
availableCommands.description: Authoring and debugging the IDE end-to-end tests in `ej-integration-tests`, which boot a sandbox IntelliJ IDEA or Android Studio with ide-starter and drive Junie as an AI Assistant ACP agent over JMX with driver-sdk. Use when adding or fixing a test in that module, when a Swing/Compose locator stops matching, or when an integration test fails only on TeamCity.

availableCommands.name: $feature-specs
availableCommands.description: Create, update, and list feature specifications under docs/specs/, and keep docs/specs/INDEX.md in sync. Supports an autonomous mode for non-interactive drafting.

availableCommands.name: $generate-release-ticket-body
availableCommands.description: Generate or refresh the description of a Junie YouTrack Release issue from verified branch metadata and its current related issues. Use as the sole writer of the Release Info and Release Notes body.

availableCommands.name: $gg-cross-review
availableCommands.description: Review the change a gg:// link names with 2–3 copies of yourself on different models, settle their disagreements, and store one merged review in gg.

availableCommands.name: $gg-cross-review-v2
availableCommands.description: Experimental v2 of gg-cross-review — 2–3 copies of yourself on different models review a gg:// link, you settle their disagreements and store one merged review.

availableCommands.name: $gg-delegate
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks you to delegate a task to worker agents through gg — prepare a worktree, brief a worker and start it (it shows its instructions and result in its own console; wait for it and check its result only when asked); also the protocol a worker started by gg follows.

availableCommands.name: $gg-overview
availableCommands.description: Use when the user says gg-overview, or asks to visualise, present or walk them through a result in gg — temporary notes on the exact lines plus an overview whose links open the code.

availableCommands.name: $gg-overview-v2
availableCommands.description: Experimental v2 of gg-overview — present a result in gg as notes plus an overview whose links open the code. Only when the user types /gg-overview-v2.

availableCommands.name: $gg-review
availableCommands.description: Review the change a gg:// link names and store the review in gg — a summary plus per-file remarks — with gg review save.

availableCommands.name: $gg-review-v2
availableCommands.description: Experimental v2 of gg-review — review the change a gg:// link names and store the review in gg with gg review save.

availableCommands.name: $ij-debugger
availableCommands.description: Debugger-first runtime root-cause analysis for JVM code in IntelliJ IDEA. Use when runtime state or control-flow evidence is needed (values, branches, call order, reachability), when the question spans long call chains across many files, or when the user explicitly requests the debugger. Evidence comes from logpoints/breakpoints, stepping, stacks, runtime values, expression evaluation, and control-flow observations.

availableCommands.name: $junie-cli-acp-integrations-tests
availableCommands.description: Test standalone Junie CLI behavior exposed over ACP using the in-process integration suite, isolated fixtures, in-memory JSON-RPC transport, and mock IDE/LLM servers. Use when changing ACP capabilities, authentication, sessions, prompts, notifications, permissions, elicitations, cancellation, steering, configuration options, or LLM routing.

availableCommands.name: $junie-cli-configuration
availableCommands.description: Use when changing Junie CLI `config.json` loading or merging, configuration flags, `settings.json` persistence, or precedence between effective configuration and persisted settings.

availableCommands.name: $junie-cli-docs
availableCommands.description: Complete documentation for using Junie CLI in the terminal. Use this skill when the user asks about Junie itself, its features, configuration, where agent sessions/settings/logs are located, or CLI commands.

availableCommands.name: $junie-cli-ga-analytics
availableCommands.description: Use when querying Junie CLI usage analytics, including GA builds, in the BigQuery table `junie-prod.ingrazzio_data_prod.cli_usage` in `europe-west4`.

availableCommands.name: $junie-cli-host-lifecycle
availableCommands.description: Use when changing Junie CLI task-to-host routing, application or process composition, a JunieHost implementation, startup, shutdown, or adding a host. Not for ordinary TUI view work or project/session lifecycle inside an existing host.

availableCommands.name: $junie-cli-integration-tests
availableCommands.description: Use when writing integration tests for standalone Junie CLI with real TUI, isolated fixtures, virtual terminal, and LLM mocks.

availableCommands.name: $junie-cli-macos-terminal-blackbox
availableCommands.description: Validate Junie CLI behavior that specifically depends on iTerm2, Ghostty, or Terminal.app, including real window rendering, focus, resize, and physical input. Use only when tmux cannot prove the terminal-emulator-specific claim.

availableCommands.name: $junie-cli-themes
availableCommands.description: Use when creating or reviewing a Junie CLI color theme file for ~/.junie/themes, or when changing the theme system itself - theme tokens (ThemeToken, AppThemeStyles), the palette (ThemePalette), the built-in dark and light themes, theme file parsing and validation (ThemeFile, ThemeCatalog), or the Auto theme. For choosing which token a view uses, read junie-cli-ui instead.

availableCommands.name: $junie-cli-tui-blackbox-smoke
availableCommands.description: Run the real Junie CLI in tmux for deterministic blackbox validation of textual and TUI behavior. Use for live visible proof after CLI changes; use CLI integration tests for code-level automation and the macOS terminal blackbox skill for emulator-specific behavior.

availableCommands.name: $junie-cli-ui
availableCommands.description: Design, implement, review, or maintain any user-visible Junie CLI TUI screen or component, including view-model separation, event handling, delegated focus, tabs, layout, alignment, lists, prompts, shortcut hints, and static or dynamic content. Load for every Junie CLI UI-related change.

availableCommands.name: $junie-cli-versioning
availableCommands.description: Explains how Junie CLI versions are allocated, propagated from CI into the binary, and rendered in user-facing surfaces. Use this skill when touching release-branch creation, TeamCity version parameters, generated BuildConfig, or any code that reads `productVersion` / `marketingVersion`.

availableCommands.name: $junie-cross-review
availableCommands.description: Coordinate independent subagent reviews of local changes, a branch diff, or the last commit; use when you want multiple reviewers to check the same change.

availableCommands.name: $junie-model-awareness
availableCommands.description: List currently available models by name to help developers choose a model for a new subagent; use whenever the user wants to choose, pick, or select models or model IDs for subagents, reviewers, cross-review, or parallel agents, or asks which models are available; never changes the parent or saved model selection.

availableCommands.name: $junie-model-awareness-maintenance
availableCommands.description: Use when changing model or provider definitions, naming conventions, or availability rules that may affect the generated junie-model-awareness skill, its maker grouping, generation ordering, compact/full catalogs, or CI gating; not for listing available models or switching the active model.

availableCommands.name: $junie-project-lifecycle
availableCommands.description: Use when changing Junie CLI project creation, live-project registration or teardown, session resume/switching, foreground/background ownership, or per-root configuration for subagents and multi-repository workspaces. Not for project path storage alone or ordinary session-event features.

availableCommands.name: $junie-project-paths
availableCommands.description: Use when adding or changing project-scoped Junie files or directories, resolving `.junie` paths, or migrating consumers to `JunieProjectPaths`; not for Junie Home, explicit sources, or additional ACP roots.

availableCommands.name: $junie-remote-bridge
availableCommands.description: Use when changing Junie remote-mode inbound commands, outbound frames, domain-to-wire mappings, sequencing or replay, WebSocket transport, or the TypeScript bridge schema.

availableCommands.name: $junie-session-feature-architecture
availableCommands.description: Guidelines for adding new Junie CLI session features through the event pipeline, projections, effects, read models, and view models instead of growing JunieSessionRuntime or MutableSessionState.

availableCommands.name: $link-issues-to-release
availableCommands.description: Synchronize a Junie YouTrack Release issue with issues whose Junie Release field matches it, including safe stale-link cleanup and one generated body refresh. Use when asked to link or resynchronize a release.

availableCommands.name: $llm-exception-handling
availableCommands.description: Guidelines for managing exception handling in LLM calls and mapping provider errors to internal LlmException types.

availableCommands.name: $llm-proxies-and-models
availableCommands.description: Guidelines for understanding Junie's LLM models and proxies architecture and configuration.

availableCommands.name: $module-naming-consistency
availableCommands.description: Audit naming and contract consistency within a module by statically tracing API and framework entry points through declared interfaces and actual implementations to the module boundary. Start from module sources, not a pre-existing report. Create one Markdown document containing the complete call trace, evidence-based naming problems, and an actionable refactoring brief with measurable acceptance criteria. Use for naming, responsibility, type ownership and nesting, and semantic clarity reviews, not for implementing the refactoring or running the application.

availableCommands.name: $pr-vcs-architecture
availableCommands.description: Architecture rules for PR review VCS data flow, local git operations, and VCS provider abstractions in the PrStructureAgent and ChatReviewAgent pipeline, plus CodeReviewIssueAgent local scope resolution.

availableCommands.name: $proofreading
availableCommands.description: Proofread or revise Junie UI text using JetBrains capitalization, punctuation, and concise-writing conventions. Use for labels, actions, tooltips, notifications, dialogs, errors, shortcuts, and other user-facing copy; preserve established product terminology.

availableCommands.name: $pull-requests
availableCommands.description: Organize changes, branches and pull requests as single logical changes (PRs are mandatory here). Use before implementing code changes, opening, updating, stacking or describing a PR, or reviewing one. Size is a secondary signal checked at 200 and 400 added production lines. Not for Junie's PR review code (pr-vcs-architecture).

availableCommands.name: $release-flow
availableCommands.description: Shared Junie release terminology and workflow across TeamCity branch allocation, technical and marketing versions, YouTrack Release issues, link synchronization, and ACP GA promotion. Use for release orchestration or when another release skill needs canonical identifiers.

availableCommands.name: $reviewing-with-gg
availableCommands.description: Use when reviewing code changes in a repository where the gg CLI is available — inspect diffs and leave anchored review notes with gg note.

availableCommands.name: $session-history
availableCommands.description: Use when a task refers to earlier Junie work — continuing, recalling, or locating a previous session, task, or decision across past sessions, or when the task mentions a concrete session id or a junie://sessions/<session_id> link. Read history from Junie Home under ~/.junie/sessions (the index.jsonl catalog first, then a session's transcript.md). Not for the current live session's own scrollback.

availableCommands.name: $skills-service-dev
availableCommands.description: Guidelines for modifying and testing the SkillsService and its associated tests.

availableCommands.name: $statistics
availableCommands.description: Add or change analytics and FUS events in core/analytics, including event identifiers, recorder fields, generated scheme updates, and validation. Use when modifying analytics event definitions, appenders, recorders, or FUS schema generation.

availableCommands.name: $teamcity-build-investigation
availableCommands.description: How to investigate failing TeamCity builds at matterhorn.internal.teamcity.cloud using the TeamCity MCP and/or the REST API via curl --netrc, without ever exposing ~/.netrc credentials.

availableCommands.name: $teamcity-dsl
availableCommands.description: Guidelines for working with TeamCity Kotlin DSL configurations and CI/CD scripts in the .teamcity/ci module.

availableCommands.name: $testable-cli-views
availableCommands.description: Design and test Junie CLI TUI view and view-model boundaries under ej-app/cli-standalone, including UI-ready state, focused view tests, and gold output. Use junie-cli-ui alongside it for every visible layout, wording, or interaction decision; not for session event architecture or live blackbox testing.

availableCommands.name: $unlink-mismatched-release-issues
availableCommands.description: Remove only verified stale relates-to links from a Junie YouTrack Release issue when a related issue's junie release field no longer matches. Use for release consistency checks or as the cleanup stage of link-issues-to-release.

availableCommands.name: $using-gg
availableCommands.description: Use when performing git operations (status, commit, pull, push, branch switch, stash, worktrees) in a repository where the gg CLI is available.

availableCommands.name: $youtrack-management
availableCommands.description: Create or update issues in the JUNIE YouTrack project, including fields, assignment, release placement, and state transitions. Use only when the user requests a YouTrack read or mutation; inspect live project fields and available connector schemas before acting.
